text: Banks, RBI, and UPI apps never ask you to share your OTP, PIN, CVV, or password.
You never need to enter a UPI PIN to receive money. Entering a UPI PIN always deducts money from your account.
Collect requests on UPI apps are used to request money from you, not to send money to you.
KYC updates are strictly done through official banking apps, websites, or physical branch visits, never via unverified SMS links.
Report cyber fraud and financial crimes immediately at the official National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal: cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.
Report suspicious calls or SMS messages through the Sanchar Saathi (Chakshu) portal by the Department of Telecommunications.
No genuine government agency, police, or CBI will ever conduct a digital arrest over a video call or ask for money to avoid legal action.
The Income Tax Department does not send links via SMS or WhatsApp asking you to claim your refund. Refunds are credited directly to pre-validated bank accounts.
TRAI (Telecom Regulatory Authority of India) does not block or deactivate mobile numbers. Any message claiming TRAI will block your number is fake.
Always verify website links by manually typing the official website URL into your browser rather than clicking on links received in SMS or WhatsApp.
Be cautious of messages creating a false sense of urgency, such as threats of account suspension, blocking, or immediate legal action.
URL shorteners (like bit.ly, tinyurl) or domains with cheap TLDs (.xyz, .top, .icu) are frequently used by scammers to hide malicious websites.
Genuine job offers or companies do not ask you to pay a registration fee or processing fee to secure a job or interview.
Legitimate lotteries or prize distributions do not require you to pay an advance tax, processing fee, or courier charge to claim your winnings.
Electricity boards do not send SMS warnings from personal mobile numbers threatening immediate power disconnection.
Customer care numbers found on random Google searches or social media may be fake. Always use numbers listed on official websites or the back of your bank card.
Banks do not send SMS messages containing raw IP addresses instead of official domain names.
Legitimate bank alerts will often include a standard warning not to share your OTP or PIN with anyone.
Do not install remote access apps (like AnyDesk or TeamViewer) if asked by someone claiming to be customer support.
Always double-check the sender ID of an SMS. Scammers often use generic sender names that look similar to official ones.
